measurement.parity: every distance checked equal to the canonical module in tools/proofs/202608311910-neon-substation-links.proof.mjs

ported_from.arithmetic: electrical arithmetic is checked independently on six sizing cases; financial arithmetic is checked against four fixtures produced by executing the original modules directly
deliberate_differences: one Earth radius: the sandbox measures on 6378.137 but builds geometry with turf.destination on 6371.0088, mixing two radii inside one drawing; the Atlas ships no turf and every operation here is canonical
grab rather than mode-switch: the array is dragged, rotation has a handle, route vertices are dragged, inserted and removed without a commit step
the electron flow runs along the collectors and the export cable in the direction power flows

central AC sizing is corrected, not carried: gis-sld-v5-calculations.js line 147 computes total_blocks * central_skid_mva * inv_per_mv, but total_blocks already contains inv_per_mv, so the inverters sharing a skid enter the answer squared, and a count of inverters is multiplied by a transformer rating. The executable original defaults use one inverter per skid, where the square is latent and both paths state 70.4 MW. An explicit two-inverter stress reports 211.2 MW in the original where the inverters total 105.6 MW and the skids 52.8 MVA; a 3-inverter stress reports 1425.6 against 158.4. The Atlas reports the smaller nameplate and names the limiting element.
ported_from.reverted_divergence: z_strings was briefly changed from the original 18 to 23 here, reasoning that 18 gives a block DC/AC of 0.945. That was done without checking the reference, which is explicit that 28 inverters at 352 kVA make 9,856 kVA "before transformer and grid limitations" - the oversizing is the design. Reverted. A port does not improve its reference by guessing. The reconciler that implemented that reasoning was then left behind uncalled; the Codex source gate flagged it as a stop-ship and it was right. Dead code that assigns to a reference input is one handler away from silently rewriting the design. Deleted, and gated against.

boot.trigger: whichever of style.load or load arrives first, then an 8s timer
boot.why: map.once("load") fires only after a frame is painted, so a basemap that never serves tiles stopped the grid maths installing at all; observed live with style.json, tiles.json and the sprite all at 200 and not one vector tile fetched
boot.independence: the distances are arithmetic over substation coordinates and need no map; layers need a parsed style, not a frame
boot.refuses: to boot with no style at all, which would fail on the first addSource

status_surface.why: a black map is indistinguishable from a broken one, and the Atlas boots a 35.7 MB query engine before it can answer anything
status_surface.waiting: Loading the grid data - the distances need it.
status_surface.failed: The grid data has not finished loading, so no distances can be measured yet. This is usually the network rather than the project.
status_surface.retry: re-runs the arrival, not the page: a reload on a phone pays for the whole engine again and the deep link is in the URL either way
status_surface.sizing: min(92vw, 420px) - the viewport, not a desktop column
status_surface.mobile_first: Vikram, 2026-08-31: build for the phone first and let it scale up, because the link that reaches most readers arrives in a WhatsApp message

label_glyphs.symptom: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'width') once per rendered frame; 4,218 on a cold load here, 50+ in about 20 seconds on mounting the layout, seen independently by the Codex session
label_glyphs.cause: a symbol layer with no glyph atlas -- either the style carries no glyphs endpoint, or it has one and the assumed font is not served by it; the font was named literally rather than taken from the style that has to serve it
label_glyphs.fix: ask the style: no glyphs endpoint means no labels, which is a quiet map rather than a broken one; otherwise borrow a font the style already labels with, because that one is definitely served
label_glyphs.why_it_matters_on_a_phone: an exception per frame is a main thread that never idles: heat, battery, and a page that stops answering touches
label_glyphs.second_half: having a glyphs endpoint is not the same as reaching it: the style declared tiles.basemaps.cartocdn.com/fonts on the same CDN that had just returned 200 for style.json and then served no vector tiles at all, which gives the identical null atlas and 5,362 exceptions in thirty seconds
label_glyphs.pre_flight: one fetch of the 0-255 range, the same request the renderer would make; no answer means no labels, and the layer is never added

card_reuse.reported: Vikram: arriving from Pipeline News and then clicking another solar pixel gives a card that is not sized correctly
card_reuse.cause: the popup element is reused between selections and nothing this cartridge wrote onto a card was ever taken off: the max-height computed for the previous card's contents, gridatlas-free if it had been freed, the --gx/--gy it was parked at, the minimised state; and addCardBar returned early once the bar existed, so the only call to boundCardToMap on that path never ran again
card_reuse.rule: geometry is per selection, content is not: the bar, its listeners and the drag handlers are kept, because rebuilding them costs a card that can no longer be moved

gb_decade.reads: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ventusltd/data-gb-electricity/d310e3cec8cd14bc7cd3eef1e37037197bcb0798/derived/price-decade-rollup.json (pinned by the pinned-products module and verified against sha256 18da5059c93cf09f6036bfcaabf56afaedf16d5f03e664c3cf0b0cff1dca970d before any value is rendered)
gb_decade.why_there: "data before charts": a consumer reads a data product that already sits clean and never owns source data or becomes a second source of truth. data-gb-electricity owns the Parquet and refreshes monthly on a schedule that is still running
gb_decade.supersedes: an earlier copy derived inside globalgrid2050, which was a second definition of the same numbers and is retired
gb_decade.size: 4 kB rollup against roughly a hundred megabytes of settlement periods
gb_decade.headline: the lowest settlement period of the decade was -185.33 GBP/MWh on 2023-07-17, a July day and so peak solar
gb_decade.solar: absent from the product by decision, and the panel says so: PVLive has not been taken into the data repository, and filling the gap from elsewhere would make a second source of truth
gb_decade.contract: requires data-gb-electricity.price-decade-rollup.v2 before rendering any value; a v1 or malformed product fails closed with no numeric values
gb_decade.exactness: the negative-day share keeps numerator and denominator visible (580 of 3,339, 17.37% in the pinned fixture); partial years are labelled from the owner's explicit calendar coverage, replacing the 360-day heuristic; the record low carries exact settlement-period and UTC identity
gb_decade.boundary_tightened: the panel no longer infers peak solar, curtailment or export limitation from the record low's date or sign - an earlier version said "a July day, which is peak solar", and that was an inference, which this estate does not make on a card
gb_decade.freshness: fetched with no-cache: revalidated on every open, never pinned to the first version this browser happened to see. force-cache held the panel on v1 for hours after the owner published v2, watched live

capacity_names.now: DC, inverter AC and export are named separately; the design ratio is DC over inverter AC, the export ratio is DC over the limit, and a disagreement between the stated and achieved ratio is stated

three_ratios.design: array DC MWp / inverter AC MW - what DC/AC means
three_ratios.export: array DC MWp / export MVA - what drives clipping
three_ratios.headroom: inverter AC MW / export MVA - how hard the inverters are pushed

dash_atlas.reported_by: the Codex session's LineAtlas cardinality gate
dash_atlas.fault: MapLibre rasterises every distinct line-dasharray into its LineAtlas and keeps it for the life of the map; a continuously varying dasharray asks for a new entry sixty times a second and the atlas runs out of space in about twenty seconds
dash_atlas.distinct_from: the glyph fault fixed in v9.21 and v9.22 — a different cause with a similar symptom, which is why closing one did not close the other
dash_atlas.fix: 24 patterns built once and frozen, cycled; measured at 24 distinct over 100,000 frames
dash_atlas.call_sites: a dash is written only when the quantised pattern changes; measured 3,168 writes in 3,600 frames, a 1.1x reduction rather than the 3.5x first claimed here - the saving grows with frame rate. The atlas bound is the substantive fix; this is tidiness on top of it

voltage_units.contract: OSM `voltage` is volts at every magnitude; an explicit `kv` property is already kilovolts. Magnitude is not the unit.
voltage_units.was: anything over 1,000 treated as volts, anything under as kilovolts
voltage_units.audited_by: the Codex session, against the pinned 5,800-feature payload
voltage_units.impact: 229 features (3.95%) carry a token below 1,000 and every one was misread; 204 displayed a primary above 400 kV, which does not exist on this network
voltage_units.why_750: DC traction supplies at railway depots, so a third rail was shown as a 750 kV substation
voltage_units.note: a bare 33 under `voltage` is now 33 volts and falls out of scope; Codex confirmed the pinned payload contains no such token, so nothing real is lost by obeying the contract

mobile_pointer.dom_fix: Pointer Events with pointer capture on the card and panel handles; no document-wide move listeners are recreated when the panel redraws

mobile_pointer.containment: the whole card width is clamped to the map, the panel is bounded by top and bottom, short landscape controls scroll, search results are viewport bounded, and primary panel controls are 44 CSS pixels

arrival_identity.latent_fault_fixed: Number(null) is 0, so a link with no coordinates passed the finite guard as Null Island; only the technology guard was accidentally stopping links being drawn to 0,0

arrival_identity.one_resolver: the search lane owns identity resolution against the pinned register parquet; this lane only consumes what it publishes
arrival_identity.budget: 120s, because the identity lane boots a 35.7 MB query engine first on a cold phone; terminal FAILED or ABSENT is honoured immediately

arrival_surface.reported_by: Vikram, phone, 13:01: fullscreen still computed nothing, and the normal page is clutter fighting a small map
arrival_surface.budget_relearned: v9.44 waited 120s for the identity lane; a cold phone boots the 35.7 MB query engine first and exceeded it, so the lane gave up permanently and the card opened with nothing computed. The wait now runs until RESOLVED, FAILED or ABSENT, with a ten-minute last-resort stop for a lane that died silently
arrival_surface.fullscreen: an arrival on a touch screen enters the shell's own fullscreen - Vikram's design: arrive in full screen mode with the clutter minimised; the tray keeps the tool buttons collapsed

arrival_card.reported_by: Vikram, phone: worked on Botley West, 'doesn't work on other lines of solar farms on pipelinenews'
arrival_card.measured: Exact Pipeline 0144 census: 2,430 of 8,743 unique clickable REPD refs are absent from the active-register snapshot; 6,313 match it. The missing set includes inactive and wider-fleet schemes that Pipeline legitimately links. Botley West happens to be present
